focus: PortraitHeadMesh original synthetic topology, outward normals, bounded BVH, ray minimum distance and degenerate triangles
review_type: remote static source and test review

checks.details: Read AGENTS.md, the eight requested startup documents and m02-m03-code-v2 acceptance contract at the pinned revision. Current state keeps M03 active; this review makes no gate-completion claim.

Source generates one synthetic head from a fixed profile and local facial displacements. Longitude wraps modulo 64. The 42 latitude bands produce two triangles per quad; coincident pole triangles are rejected. The resulting 5248 nondegenerate faces follows from 2*42*64 - 2*64 and is a source-derived count, not an executed observation. Bottom and top fans retain the same outward orientation as the regular strips.

Vertex normals use tangent cross vertical, with explicit lower/upper pole normals. Triangles use matching outward edge winding. Interpolated normals require finite nonzero normalization and agreement with the geometric hemisphere and viewing ray; otherwise the outward geometric normal is used. Interior rays preserve outward normals instead of flipping toward the camera. Test source compares finite unit normals, face hemispheres and interior exit direction.

Immutable standard mesh and hierarchy are constructed once. Each node bounds its full triangle range before subdivision; median splitting strictly shrinks each non-leaf range until at most eight faces remain. Fixed 5248-face input implies at most ten split levels below the root. AABB intersection handles near-parallel axes and uses conservative 1e-10 padding. Independent oracle test source compares exterior views, misses, poles, seam/shared edges and grazing rays without sharing BVH traversal.

Triangle intersections require t >= minimum and t < maximum. Both nearest-hit and occlusion paths use those bounds. Tie search is clamped to original maximum; the returned distance remains the minimum even when an incident outward face supplies a preferable normal. Test source explicitly brackets independent hit distances, tests empty/reversed intervals, checks excluded upper endpoints and nextUp-sized intervals, and covers coincident silhouette faces.

Construction rejects squared area <= 1e-24, including duplicated pole faces. Intersection rejects determinants with magnitude <= 1e-14 before division. Normalization requires finite positive length. Oracle construction independently removes zero-area pole triangles and asserts equal face counts. The private fixed mesh initializer does not expose arbitrary imported topology.

Reviewed assertions for the declared 210 exterior rays, 63 seam/pole/edge/grazing rays, 12 interior rays and 15 finite-segment cases. Counts describe test code only; no passing runtime result is claimed.

limitations: Host was unavailable. No shell scripts, Swift tests, builds, renderers, benchmarks or native/device runs were executed.
Remote source and recursive tree were read at the exact assigned revision; local branch, worktree status and uncommitted changes could not be inspected.
Review is bounded static analysis and does not prove all numerical inputs, photographic fidelity, visual acceptance or milestone acceptance.
Rendering width, camera framing and photometry were excluded as assigned. The render-level exact-silhouette test was not separately re-reviewed for those excluded concerns.
The test oracle independently checks intersection/traversal while sharing prescribed mesh vertices and topology; the topology conclusion here additionally relies on direct source inspection.
conclusion: No must-fix defect identified in the assigned source/test scope at the pinned revision.
